puck_slide_predict — DRIVE puck op

• Data kinds: signal × signal × table × scalar → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.puck_slide_predict(p0, v0, table: 'dict', t_end: 'float', *, model: 'str' = 'coulomb', max_bounces: 'int' = 50, goals: 'bool' = True, t0: 'float' = 0.0) -> 'dict' (to call the implementation directly, import puck; puck.puck_slide_predict(p0, v0, table: 'dict', t_end: 'float', *, model: 'str' = 'coulomb', max_bounces: 'int' = 50, goals: 'bool' = True, t0: 'float' = 0.0) -> 'dict'; from the registry, opsdrive.get("puck_slide_predict"))

Usage

Chains the puck path in closed form: constant direction and uniform deceleration per segment (wall to wall), puck_wall_bounce at the walls.

Clock: p₀ and v₀ are the state at time t0 (default 0), and t_end is the length from there. Segment times and crossing times are absolute times including t0 (if you pass the t_ref of velocity estimation as t0, crossing times come out on the camera's clock). model = "coulomb" (a = μg, with stopping) / "viscous" (a = (c/m) v, the damping in the Challenge's MJCF) / "none" (no friction). The time of hitting a wall is the closed-form solution of d(τ) = required distance (a quadratic equation or a logarithm). If goals=True, |y| < goal_half on the end walls is a goal (ends there, event "goal"). When the speed reaches 0, "stop"; timeout is "end". Return value {"segments": [{"t0","t1","p0","v0","u","s0","event"}, …], "t_end", "p_end", "v_end", "n_bounces", "events"}. Positions along the path via puck_state_at. Agrees with the mirror method (puck_mirror_path, no friction, e = kₜ = 1) to 1e-9 (gate).
